groundingLine: Human-facing principles can inform AI design
groundingNote: : a hypothesis to test, not a law.

sunlight.title: Sunlight
sunlight.script: We are one level down, in the sunlit zone. Here we decide two things: when a task may deserve a skill, and how to describe it so people or platforms can find it.

borrowed-principles.title: Borrowed principles
borrowed-principles.script: From here on I borrow principles from engineering, information architecture and UX. They can suggest useful ways to design for AI, but transfer is a hypothesis to test, not a law.

why-a-rule-of-thumb.title: Why a rule of thumb
why-a-rule-of-thumb.script: The model's output depends on its training and the context the product supplies, like a capable newcomer with a briefing. The human-facing principles are useful hypotheses, but they can break; the next Slide's notes show where.
